chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and Bukayr and Fadl and Muhammad and Burayd, from one of them (peace be upon them both), who said:
"Indeed, the grandfather, when with the paternal brothers, becomes like one of the brothers, as long as they have reached adulthood."

He said: I said, 'A man leaves behind his brother from his father and his mother, and his paternal grandmother' or I said, 'his grandfather and his brother from his father, or his brother from his father and his mother.' He said, 'The wealth is shared between them, and if there are two brothers, or [the estate is] a hundred thousand, he has the share of one of the brothers.'

He said: I said, 'A man leaves behind his grandfather and his sister.' He said, 'For the male is the share of two females.' And if there are two sisters, then half is for the grandfather and the other half is for the two sisters. And if there are more than that, then it is according to this calculation.

And if he leaves behind brothers and sisters from father and mother, or from father and a grandfather, then the grandfather is one of the brothers, so the wealth is shared between them, 'For the male is the share of two females.'
And Zurarah said: 'This is from what was not taken against me; I have heard it from his father and from him before that, and there is no doubt or difference among us regarding it.'

key_terms.اَلْأَخُ لِأَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ: Full brother (sharing both father and mother)
key_terms.اَلْإِخْوَةُ مِنَ اَلْأَبِ: Paternal brothers (siblings sharing the same father)
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ اَلْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is the share of two females (standard Quranic inheritance ratio)

ai.seo_question: How is the paternal grandfather's share calculated when inheriting alongside full or paternal siblings?
ai.summary: This hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies the specific status of the paternal grandfather (al-Jadd) when competing with siblings, establishing him as a 'single brother' (kif al-akh) who receives a share equal to one male sibling, distinct from the fixed fractional shares. The narration highlights the consensus (ijma') among the scholars of the Ahl al-Bayt on this matter, resolving potential ambiguities in the application of the 'for the male is the share of two females' principle in complex family structures.
